themes_detail.label: Elevator Crisis in Public Housing
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints in CD 501 spiked to 5 complaints THIS WEEK, up 3,900% from a baseline of 0.1 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.74), suggesting a sudden, widespread failure affecting residents' access to homes and services.
evidence: 5 elevator complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 per-week average over prior 8 weeks (3,900% spike)
Z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Affects vertical access in buildings across district, particularly public housing complexes
reporting_angles: Which NYCHA buildings are experiencing outages? How many residents are affected and for how long?
Has NYCHA's maintenance or funding changed recently? Are service calls being ignored?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints hit 9 reports LAST WEEK, up 1,100% from an 8-week baseline of 0.8 per week (z-score: 9.95), concurrent with a 1,900% spike in noise complaints from parks, suggesting organized or concentrated illicit activity in public spaces.
evidence: 9 drug activity complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 per-week average (1,100% spike, z-score: 9.95)
Concurrent 5 noise-from-park complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 per-week average (1,900% spike, z-score: 10.97)
Pattern suggests concentrated activity in specific parks; community board has repeatedly requested youth prevention services
reporting_angles: Which parks are hotspots? Have dealers moved into specific locations? What do residents and park users report?
Is NYPD enforcement present? Are there gaps in park policing or lighting that enable this activity?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting and Litter Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints peaked 2 weeks ago at 11 (up 700% from 1.4 weekly baseline) and litter basket complaints hit 7 (up 833% from 0.8 weekly baseline) at the same time, signaling a coordinated public-space degradation or advertising/graffiti campaign affecting neighborhood cleanliness.
evidence: 11 illegal posting complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.4 per-week average (700% spike, z-score: 8.66)
7 litter basket complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 per-week average (833% spike, z-score: 7.54)
Timing overlap suggests coordinated issue (posting campaign, event, or contractor work)
reporting_angles: What was being posted? Political ads, commercial posters, or graffiti? Is there a single source?
Did sanitation collection fail at the same time, or is this about overflow from illegal dumping or events?

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping in Residences Spike
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints hit 23 reports 2 WEEKS AGO, up 411% from a baseline of 4.5 per week (z-score: 7.72), suggesting either a concentrated enforcement period or increased tenant frustration with secondhand smoke seeping into units—an issue affecting indoor air quality in multi-unit buildings.
evidence: 23 smoking/vaping complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.5 per-week average (411% spike, z-score: 7.72)
Spike corresponds with broader public-space quality issues (posting, litter, noise) suggesting environmental degradation period
Likely affects multi-family housing units where smoke intrusion is a persistent complaint
reporting_angles: Is this about indoor smoking violating lease agreements, or outdoor smoking affecting nearby residents?
Were there enforcement campaigns or awareness campaigns that drove complaints up?

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Improvement
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints dropped 53% THIS WEEK to 19 reports vs. a baseline of 40.8 per week (z-score: -4.9), bucking the trend of other public-space degradation spikes and potentially indicating successful intervention or seasonal improvement.
evidence: 19 unsanitary condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 40.8 per-week average (53% decline, z-score: -4.9)
Countertrend: other public-space issues (posting, litter, noise, drugs) are spiking, so decline is anomalous
May reflect seasonal shift, successful sanitation intervention, or reporting lag
reporting_angles: Did the city deploy additional sanitation crews or enforcement recently?
Is this a weather-related shift, or is there an underlying intervention worth replicating?
